name: midnight-passport-workspace

scripts.build: npm run build --workspace passport-demo-backend && npm run build --workspace passport-demo && npm run build --workspace passport-profile-client
scripts.deploy:passport: VITE_RAFFLE_URL=https://raffle.midnightpassport.com VITE_FUNDER_URL=https://funder.midnightpassport.com npm run build --workspace passport-demo && node scripts/build-vercel-output.mjs examples/passport-demo && cd examples/passport-demo && vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod --yes
scripts.deploy:raffle: VITE_PASSPORT_ORIGIN=https://midnightpassport.com npm run build --workspace examples/raffle-demo && node scripts/build-vercel-output.mjs examples/raffle-demo && cd examples/raffle-demo && vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod --yes
scripts.deploy:template: cd examples/passport-app-template && VITE_PASSPORT_ORIGIN=https://midnightpassport.com npm run build && cd ../.. && node scripts/build-vercel-output.mjs examples/passport-app-template && cd examples/passport-app-template && vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod --yes
scripts.deploy:hub: npm run build --workspace passport-app-hub && node scripts/build-vercel-output.mjs examples/passport-app-hub && cd examples/passport-app-hub && vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod --yes
scripts.deploy:docs: npm run build --workspace passport-docs && node scripts/build-vercel-output.mjs examples/passport-docs && cd examples/passport-docs && vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod --yes

//dependencies: `compact-runtime` is pinned HERE so that npm's hoisting is a decision
rather than an accident, and it is pinned to the LEDGER-9 one.
Why it has to be decided at all: a generated Compact contract module opens
the bundler and Node resolve that specifier from the MODULE's directory,
walking upwards — so which copy a contract gets is decided by where the
contract file sits, not by which workspace asked for it. On top of that,
midnight-js decodes contract state through `ChargedState`, and two copies
of the runtime are two `ChargedState` classes: an `instanceof` check then
fails on objects that are correct in every other respect.
So both stacks are made coherent from opposite ends. The root holds the
ledger-9 runtime, which is what `examples/passport-demo` and the ledger-9
midnight-js packages hoisted alongside it all share — ONE copy, including
stagenet`. `examples/passport-funder` names 0.16.0 in its own dependencies,
so it gets a nested copy that its bundle resolves first at run time; that
is the version the ledger-8 contract build it loads demands.
//overrides: Two Midnight stacks live in this workspace at once and must both resolve.
5.0.0-beta.6) for stagenet; examples/passport-funder stays on ledger-8
(wallet-sdk-* v3/v4, midnight-js 4.0.4) because preview is where it runs.
Every conflicting package is pinned to an exact version on both sides, so
npm nests the loser under the workspace that asks for it rather than
hoisting one over the other. The single override below is SCOPED BY
which does not export Clock — the facade imports it and dies on load. 1.2.1
is the fixed publish. The ledger-8 packages request 1.1.1, which the
`@1.2.0` selector does not match, so the funder's tree is untouched. A bare
moved it and is deliberately not what is written here.
